title: Enterprise Compliance Concierge Playbook
summary: A playbook for enterprise sellers and solution engineers to act as a 'Compliance Concierge' during security-led evaluations. Focus: SOC2/ISO/HIPAA readiness, data handling promises, and unambiguous audit-log language. The goal is to shorten procurement cycles by pre-baking evidence, clear seller language, and a handoff checklist for security and legal teams.
context_and_goals: Context: increasingly, procurement and infosec teams request deep evidence (config snapshots, KMS details, audit-log retention proofs) beyond one-pagers. Goal: provide a repeatable, low-lift response pattern that maps customer asks to exact evidence artifacts we can deliver, and recommended seller language that balances speed with legal accuracy.
positioning_message: Short framing for buyers: Redwood is a production-first inference platform built for regulated workloads — we combine a hardened control plane with optional private deployments and auditable telemetry. We do not claim to be a legal compliance provider; instead we provide technical controls and evidence (SOC2 report, ISO certificate guidance, audit-log exports, KMS integration details, and deployment models) to support your compliance program.
audit_log_language:
Recommended lines to use verbatim when customers ask about audit trails:
- 'We provide immutable, timestamped audit logs that capture control-plane actions (model deployments, API key rotations, access grants) and data-plane request metadata where enabled. Logs are retained per plan and can be exported to customer SIEMs via S3/HTTPS syslog.'
- 'For Private deployments we offer customer-controlled log sinks inside your VPC; for Hosted we provide tenant-separated logs with customizable retention and on-demand exports.'
- 'We classify and document which actions are recorded (auth events, config changes, model promotions, system errors). If you need specific event types, we will confirm with engineering and provide a sample event schema and example export.'
data_handling_bullets:
Key commitments and what to avoid promising without legal sign-off:
- Commit: 'We support per-customer data isolation on Dedicated and Private options; for Hosted, data is logically separated and accessible only by authorized Redwood services.'
- Commit: 'At-rest encryption using AES-256; customer-managed keys are available via KMS/HSM integrations on Private/Dedicated deployments.'
- Avoid promising: 'We can guarantee deletion across backups within X minutes' — route to legal/infra for a confirmed SLA before committing.
customer_evidence_checklist:
Artifacts we can attach quickly (priority order):
1) SOC2 Type II redacted report (latest fiscal year)
2) ISO27001 certificate + scope statement
3) HIPAA BAAs template and HIPAA readiness checklist
4) Sample audit-log export (anonymized) and event schema
5) KMS integration guide and screenshot of key policy (redacted)
6) Network topology diagram for Private deployment (customer-facing)
7) Data residency matrix by region and retention defaults
8) Runbook excerpt showing incident escalation for data incidents
-- Note: Tag artifacts with version and date; maintain a manifest so sellers can pick the right ones for the customer.
quick_seller_scripts:
Email triage template (first response when security asks for evidence):
Hi <CISO_Name>,
Thanks for the detailed ask — we have a Compliance Concierge packet that maps common RFP questions to exact artifacts (SOC2, ISO cert, sample logs, KMS details, and deployment diagrams). I'm sharing the packet and am happy to schedule a short walk-through with our solutions engineer to go over live examples and confirm any additional event types you need captured.
Best,
<seller_name>

Meeting runbook (10–25 min):
1) 0–3 min: Introductions + confirm scope (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA focus?).
2) 3–10 min: Demo packet contents (highlight redacted SOC2, show sample log export).
3) 10–18 min: Ask clarifying questions (fields required, retention windows, SIEM integration).
4) 18–25 min: Commit next steps and delivery dates; route legal items to CS & Legal.

Objection handling snippets:
Q: 'How do you prevent model leakage via telemetry?'
A: 'Telemetry is limited to operational metadata; we do not capture full request payloads in logs unless explicitly configured. For sensitive workloads we recommend Private deployment with in-VPC control-plane and customer-managed keys.'
competitive_notes:
Observed positioning by competitors and suggested rebuttals: 
- Competitor A (managed endpoints): leans on 'single-tenant' as security shorthand. Rebuttal: 'Single-tenancy alone doesn't deliver observability or developer ergonomics — Redwood pairs isolated deployment options with first-class audit logs and exportability.'
- Competitor B (marketplace models): emphasizes 'we don't store any customer data.' Rebuttal: 'We similarly minimize retained data by default, but we go further by offering cryptographic key control, configurable log sinks, and documented audit schemas for compliance teams.'
- Competitor C (on-prem runtime): says 'you host, therefore you are compliant.' Rebuttal: 'Hosting is just one piece; we provide hardened deployment patterns, upgrade runbooks, and incident playbooks so your security team has a replicable operational model.'
legal_risk_flags:
Redlines / items to avoid in seller conversations: 
- Do not promise specific regulatory compliance outcomes (e.g., 'we are HIPAA compliant for your use case') — always route to Legal for contract-level statements.
- Don't commit to custom retention/deletion SLAs without Legal and Infra sign-off.
- Avoid public statements about irreversible immutability of logs unless immutable storage solution is part of the contract.
Flag these items early and copy the assigned Legal reviewer in replies.
measure_of_success:
KPIs for the play: 
- Reduction in average security evaluation cycle (days) for enterprise deals where playbook is used.
- % of RFP asks closed with standard packet vs. engineering time required.
- Positive feedback score from CS/SE on packet completeness.
Target: reduce evaluation time by 30% in pilot accounts within quarter.
